problem: ObjectNav is mostly formulated as one-shot exploration in unknown scenes, and prior reusable/pre-explored maps do not address that a recognized object's camera pose is a poor STOP goal, so one confident map error ends the task.
motivation: Long-lived service robots revisit the same environments for many requests, so a reusable memory should amortize perception and answer queries by retrieval. The key obstacle is an observation-to-action gap: the observation pose differs from a valid reachable stopping pose, and single-view detections are unreliable.
key_idea: Build a goal-independent topological graph once, project view-local VLM detections with depth into reachable object-centric standoffs, fuse them across independent viewpoints, and keep spatially diverse residual standoffs for sequential recovery verified by fresh RGB-D.
insight: Same-response ablations show most of the gain comes from geometry, not semantics: depth-based metric grounding raises SR 0.835 to 0.920 with identical VLM outputs (93 gains/8 losses). Fusion mainly compresses candidates (20,107 to 1,329) and lowers DTG, but is not monotonic on full data (28/22 gain/loss, SPL drops). Recovery with residual standoffs beats fused-only Top-3 (0.975 vs 0.964). Geometric density saturates at half the nodes, while semantic corruption remains damaging.
method: Goal-independent topology: fixed-seed farthest-point sampling of navigable points to 0.8 m cover radius; edges to up to 8 neighbors when navmesh geodesic is under a threshold; four cardinal RGB-D views per node.

Detection to navigable candidate: the VLM (GPT-5.4) returns per-view boxes; median depth in a 7x7 patch back-projects the object surface point, which is shifted 0.8 m toward the source camera, snapped to the navmesh, and discarded if unreachable.

Reachability-aware soft fusion: cluster same-category detections by 3D proximity (1.2 m horizontal, 1.0 m vertical) and mutual geodesic reachability (3 m); noisy-OR over independent source nodes; keep clusters with two or more sources or singletons with confidence at least 0.92.
Two-layer store: H^F holds fused representatives; H^R holds all reachable pre-fusion standoffs for recovery.
Query ranking and recovery: candidates sorted lexicographically by (-Q, graph distance); visit 1 from H^F, up to 2 later visits from H^R with at least 2 m separation; receding-path execution.

Fresh-arrival verification: four 120° RGB-D views at arrival; GPT-5.4 gives visibility, stopping-side validity and confidence; accept if confidence is at least 0.75 and depth is in [0.25, 2.5] m, else go to the next candidate.
ROS 2/Nav2 realization on a Yahboom X3 with a natural-language interface (qualitative demo only).

setting.backbone: GPT-5.4 (frozen, hosted; main); MiMo-v2.5 and Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct as controls
setting.observation: RGB-D at pre-explored graph nodes (four 120° 640x640 views per node at 1.25 m height); fresh RGB-D at arrival
setting.action_space: graph shortest-path between candidate standoff points on a navmesh (continuous navmesh paths; Nav2 goals on the real robot)
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim 0.3.3 (HM3D-Semantics v0.2); ROS 2 Humble/Nav2 for the real robot
setting.privileged: Pre-exploration: a goal-independent survey of the scene is built before the episodes; navmesh geodesic distances/reachability; official goal viewpoints are used only for evaluation. The Top-K tables use the official evaluator's stop signal; the deployable verifier does not.

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,000 episodes / 36 scenes, HM3D-Semantics v0.2 (2023 challenge episodes)

numbers.extra: pre-explored map; up to 3 destinations; official evaluator stop signal used for Top-K success

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,000 episodes; autonomous fresh-arrival verifier (no goal access)
numbers.method: SSTG-Nav raw candidates, strict dual-geometry arrival verification
numbers.extra: pre-explored map; deployable verifier; S@3 shown
numbers.evidence: Supp Table (tab:s-arrival) Raw 3 m strict dual geometry S@1 0.854, SPL@1 0.560; S@3 0.912, SPL@3 0.573

numbers_note: The paper labels its split 'HM3D-v2 full validation' (1,000 episodes); recorded as 'val'. Minival/model-control numbers appear in Tables 5 and S-rgbd but are omitted here.
results: On 1,000 HM3D-v2 validation episodes with a goal-independent pre-explored map, SSTG-Nav reaches 0.926 SR/0.586 SPL with one destination and 0.975/0.601 with fusion-aware Top-3, above the best unknown-scene method listed (ConsistNav 0.842 SR; FOM-Nav 0.479 SPL). The autonomous verifier achieves 0.912 S@3. Note that these results use a pre-explored map, so they are not directly comparable to online ObjectNav.
limitations: Single HM3D-v2 split, one hosted primary VLM, six categories, static scenes; no open-vocabulary or relational queries evaluated.
Simulator uses continuous navmesh paths with no control noise, localization drift or map change; the real robot result is qualitative only.
Top-K headline numbers use the official evaluator's success signal; the deployable verifier reaches lower SR (0.912 S@3). Fusion is not monotonic (SPL drops, and wider FoV hurts MiMo).
